חמשה עשר בשבט The Schwartzes Are Coming! Secret Journal!

When the Schwartzes came today, I sat next to Amy and showed her how fun the Shabbos table can be. I helped her with netilas yadayim, explained my dvar Torah, and shared my Hachayol magazine. A miracle happened—Amy stayed for bentching and even asked me to help her say the first paragraph!

When Alex and Benny saw Amy participating so nicely, they got interested too. There was a lot less screaming and chickpea throwing. Alex even joined my brother in singing the niggun of the week. It was a whole wonderfully different Shabbos meal.

Don't read! (Unless you can help me with my plans to become a five star general and blast

You’d never believe it. Today, Amy came on mivtzoyim with me, and even brought her friend. We gave out thirty-two packages of neshek candles.

Imagine how far our mitzvos are reaching… further than any chickpeas or gefilte fish could be thrown…like seeds that scatter in the wind and grow trees far and wide.

As I light my Shabbos candle today, I’ll picture the thirty-two women and girls we met today, each lighting their own candle.

I wonder who they will influence to do more mitzvos.

The Schwartzes are coming for the Shabbos meal this week. Oy vey.

Whenever the Schwartzes come, we have to cook all Friday because we need lots of extra food for Benny. And Benny doesn’t even eat a lot of food. He’s only two. But he sits in the highchair and throws gefilte fish and chickpeas all over the walls.

The other kids, Alex and Amy, run around yelling and jumping on the couch. It’s just chaos.

I wish I could escape to my room, but a chayol knows better than to go AWOL (that means “run away from the army.”) Especially when you need to succeed at every mission to become a five- star general—and the Shabbos table has a ton of missions.

What oh what will I do when the Schwartzes come?

Last year, in V’halachta Bidrachav, I learned that a chayol is never stuck— Hashem gives us every tool we need.

And that tool came into my hands today when my class went to Shlomie’s Farm for Tu B’Shvat.

We were peeling juicy oranges in the greenhouse when Shlomie the farmer asked us, “Do you know what the most important part of the orange tree is?”

“The seeds, of course!” I declared. “Cause each seed can grow a whole new tree with lots more fruits.”

Which made me think: We learned that a chayol is like a tree. A chayol grows seeds too—the people he or she influenced to do more mitzvos. And those people influence others to do mitzvos, too. Before you know it, the whole world is filled with people doing mitzvos.

And that’s how I’m going to get through the Shabbos meal with the Schwartzes— just wait and see!
